text:
maya.s: Heads-up — we have a customer asking if we can safely serve inference from non-EU GPUs during EU-region capacity spikes while keeping PII pinned to EU storage. Want to capture quick design tradeoffs before the RFC follow-up.

samir: Quick take: two broad options — active-active with resident KV/cache pinning, or resident-primary with remote inference-only fallback. Active-active is low-latency but complicates residency guarantees.

eli.arch: Agree. Need to be explicit about the SLA/consent model. If customer requires "data never leaves EU", fallback is impossible. If consent allows ephemeral non-EU inference (no persistent storage), we can do inference outside EU but must ensure no logs/kv/prefix caching leaves region and model variants are cleared.

maya.s: Customer's language: "PII must not leave EU at rest; transient inference ok if not persisted." So we can consider transient inference outside region, but must guarantee no KV writes, no audit logs containing PII, and KMS keys remain EU-only.

samir: That maps to a policy: ResidentDataPolicy = {persist: eu-only, ephemeral_compute_allowed: true, telemetry_strip: true}. Operationally means: route request to EU primary, if queue latency > X ms or queue_depth > Y, route to fallback pool but inject policy that strips/obfuscates PII and sets ttl=0 for any caches.

eli.arch: Important: model cache (KV cache of past tokens) can leak PII — we must disable prefix caching for fallbacks or use encrypted cache keys bound to EU KMS so they are unusable outside region. Also ensure that any fallback inference runs on instances that cannot access customer KMS or blob store.

maya.s: Can we do an enforcement gate in routing layer? e.g. something like:
```json
{
  "route_policy": "prefer_resident",
  "fallback": {
    "allowed": true,
    "constraints": ["no_kv_cache","no_persist","no_telemetry"]
  }
}
```

samir: Yep, routing gate should inject a capability header to the worker: X-ResFallback-Mode: ephemeral. Workers enforce via runtime config. Need to make sure runtime has runtime-checks, not just routing, to avoid accidental writes.

eli.arch: Runtime changes needed: 1) a runtime flag to disable KV write ops and prefix caching; 2) KMS isolation check — if the model needs EU KMS for any intermediate artifact, fallback disallowed; 3) telemetry redact pipeline at ingress.

maya.s: Ops question — how do we detect the "capacity spike"? Simple threshold on queue latency/percentile? we should avoid flapping.

samir: Use sustained window: 90th percentile latency > SLO for T seconds OR queue length > threshold for T seconds. Then promote region->fallback routing with a cool-down period and circuit-breaker style backoff.

eli.arch: Also consider cost/throughput: fallback instances may be cheaper or different model size. Need to surface model variant mapping in the routing policy so we can downgrade to a quantized variant when outside EU. That reduces cost and minimizes cache requirements.

maya.s: For audits: customers will ask for proof that their data didn't persist. We should log routing_decision and ephemeral_mode but redact PII. Maybe create an attestation event: {timestamp, tenant_id, route:eu|fallback, ephemeral:true, kms_used:false}.

samir: Ops-bot suggestion? ops-bot: Deploy-check OK. Add circuit-breaker metrics to /metrics/fallbacks and a per-tenant flag in tenant-config store "fallback_allowed": true|false. Default false for regulated tenants.

eli.arch: Edge case: A tenant uses an enterprise KMS (customer-managed) that's EU-only — we must block fallback. Mark rule: if tenant.kms_location == "EU-only" then fallback_allowed=false regardless of tenant flag.

maya.s: Perf/consistency note — when we run inference outside EU without caching, latency might improve but overall throughput may drop because no prefix reuse. Need to communicate expected degraded QPS to customer and offer pre-warm reserved Dedicated capacity as an alternative.

samir: Implementation plan for RFC follow-up:
- Define routing grammar and headers (who owns)
- Runtime enforcement points (KV, KMS checks, telemetry redaction)
- Metrics/circuit-breaker behavior and thresholds
- Tenant-config flags and enterprise defaults
- UX: console toggle + per-route opt-in with audit attestation

eli.arch: Also add tests: e2e sim that asserts no blob writes, no KMS usage, and that KV cache hits are zero for fallback flows. Automation should run against a fake EU tenant and assert policy.

maya.s: Sounds good. I'll draft the RFC and include a small decision matrix: when to allow fallback, when to refuse, and required guarantees. Anything else?

samir: Add a migration plan for existing tenants — one-time opt-in via Console for fallback, default off for enterprise/regulatory customers.

eli.arch: And include a short appendix on threat model: risks of inference-exfiltration via model weights/cache and mitigation (no persistent cache, ephemeral-only inference nodes, KMS gating).

maya.s: Great. I'll post an initial RFC tomorrow and ping infra for numbers on fallback throughput. :thumbsup:
